text:
NASA ordered Boeing’s Starliner to return uncrewed because the spacecraft experienced five reaction-control system (RCS) thruster anomalies during its docking approach, and NASA determined that these thrusters could not be guaranteed safe for the deorbit burn [Source: ev-1]. This safety concern was compounded by the fact that the thrusters could not be ground-tested in their specific flight condition [Source: ev-1].

The decision had significant implications for both the crew and the program. Astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams were stranded on the International Space Station until they returned aboard a Crew-9 Dragon capsule on March 18, 2025, resulting in an approximately 9.5-month stay aloft compared to the originally planned ~8 days [Source: ev-1]. For the Starliner program itself, this event highlighted substantial financial and operational challenges; Boeing has disclosed cumulative program losses of more than $1.5 billion by 2025 under its fixed-price contract from the 2014 Commercial Crew program (valued at about $4.2 billion for Boeing versus about $2.6 billion for SpaceX) [Source: ev-1]. Consequently, NASA’s path toward certifying Starliner remained unresolved through 2025, and Boeing announced roughly 400 job cuts in its space division that same year [Source: ev-1].
